explain.say: Every load in a building must find an unbroken route down to the ground, called the load path. It starts with the weight of the roof, the floors, the people and furniture, and even snow.

explain.say: Floor slabs pass the load sideways to beams, and beams carry it to the columns or walls. Each part hands the load on to the next, like runners in a relay race.

explain.say: Finally the foundations spread the load over enough soil or rock that the ground can push back without sinking. If any link in the path is removed, the load has nowhere to go and that part can collapse.

faq.a: A load path is the route a force takes through a structure, from where it is applied down to the ground. A good design gives every load a clear, continuous path.
asks: How do loads travel through a building?

faq.q: What loads does a building carry?
faq.a: Engineers add up the dead load, which is the weight of the structure itself, and the live load from people, furniture and vehicles, plus snow, wind and sometimes earthquakes.
asks: What is dead load and live load?
What forces act on a building?

faq.q: Why are the bottom columns thicker?
faq.a: Each column carries every floor above it, so the load builds up as you go down. The ground-floor columns of a tall building carry the most and are made thickest.
asks: Why are columns bigger at the bottom?

faq.a: Foundations spread a building's load over a wide enough area of soil, or carry it down to firm rock, so the ground does not sink or settle unevenly.

faq.q: What happens if a column is removed?
faq.a: The load it carried loses its path to the ground. Good designs give alternative paths, so neighbouring beams and columns can take over and one failure does not spread into a collapse.
asks: Can a building stand if a column fails?

facts: Engineers treat dead load, the structure's own weight, and live load, from people, furniture and snow, separately, and add safety factors to both.
In a tall building the ground-floor columns carry the weight of every floor above them.

quiz.say: In a building, which part carries a beam's load down to the foundations?
quiz.show: A beam's load goes down through the…
quiz.why: Beams pass their load to columns or load-bearing walls, which carry it down in compression to the foundations.

wrong.1: Windows are openings and carry little or no load.
wrong.2: The roof is at the top of the load path, not on the way down.
